statement: For any finite positive Borel measure mu with an atom of mass m>0 at an interior point of open interval I and any p>1, if F_eta(E)=integral eta/((t-E)^2+eta^2) dmu(t), then liminf_{eta down to 0} eta^(p-1) integral_I F_eta(E)^p dE >= m^p integral_R(1+u^2)^(-p)du. If a random finite measure has positive probability of an atom in I, its expected integrated p moment cannot remain eta-uniformly bounded along any deterministic eta_n down to zero.
assumptions: atom t0 in I of mass m>0
proof_or_counterexample: Positivity bounds F_eta below by the atom's Poisson kernel. Raising to p and substituting u=(E-t0)/eta gives the scaled integral over (I-t0)/eta, which converges to c_p. On a positive-probability atomic event the scaled samplewise liminf is positive; Fatou gives a positive lower bound for scaled expected moments.
